title: Finite algebras over a complete Noetherian local ring are products of complete local rings
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring which is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $R\to S$ be a ring map making $S$ a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $S$ is a Noetherian ring with finitely many maximal ideals, and $S$ is isomorphic to a finite product $S_1\times\dots\times S_t$ of Noetherian local rings $(S_j,\mathfrak n_j)$ each of which is $\mathfrak n_j$-adically complete. In particular, if $S$ is a domain, then $S$ is a Noetherian local ring, complete with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, and $\mathfrak n$ is the only prime ideal of $S$ whose inverse image in $R$ is $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local, line 44811), second sentence, and its proof (Lemmas Noetherian-permanence, completion-tensor, 07N9 completion-finite-extension); the 'in particular' clause: a domain has no idempotents other than 0 and 1, and primes over the maximal ideal m are maximal by integrality (Lemma 00GQ integral-going-up)

proof.text: (Notation; $S$ is Noetherian.) Write $\varphi:R\to S$ for the ring map. $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-module and $R$ is Noetherian, so $S$ is a Noetherian ring [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] (Stacks 00FN).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local), proof, first sentence (Lemma 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence)

proof.text: (The maximal ideals of $S$ are the primes over $\mathfrak m$, and there are finitely many.) Let $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ ($t\ge0$) be the prime ideals $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak m$; there are finitely many of them by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] (applied with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$; Stacks 05DR). $S$ is integral over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], so each $\mathfrak q_i$, lying over the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, is maximal [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal]. Conversely every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $S$ satisfies $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical], so $\mathfrak n$ is one of the $\mathfrak q_i$. Hence the maximal ideals of $S$ are exactly $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$, finitely many, and they are also exactly the primes of $S$ over $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0325, proof, third sentence ('the completions at its maximal ideals'), read with Lemma 07N9 (the $\mathfrak q_i$ are the primes over $\mathfrak p$, finite by Lemma 05DR) and Lemma 00GS (2) (primes over a maximal ideal of an integral extension are maximal)

proof.text: ($S$ is $\mathfrak mS$-adically complete.) $S$ is a finitely generated module over the Noetherian ring $R$, which is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] (with $J=\mathfrak m$, $N=S$) the canonical map $\iota_S:S\to\varprojlim_nS/\mathfrak m^nS$, $s\mapsto(s\bmod\mathfrak m^nS)_n$, is bijective. Here the $R$-submodule $\mathfrak m^nS$ (generated by the $a\cdot s=\varphi(a)s$, $a\in\mathfrak m^n$, $s\in S$) is the ideal $\varphi(\mathfrak m^n)S=(\mathfrak mS)^n$ of $S$ ($\mathfrak m^n$ is additively generated by products $a_1\cdots a_n$ with $a_i\in\mathfrak m$, and $\varphi(a_1\cdots a_n)s=\varphi(a_1)\cdots\varphi(a_n)s$). So $\iota_S$ is the canonical ring map from $S$ to its $\mathfrak mS$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and it is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0325, proof, second sentence ('As an $R$-module $S$ is complete by Lemma completion-tensor', Lemma 00MA)

proof.text: ($S$ is the product of the completions at its maximal ideals.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$: there is a ring isomorphism between the $\mathfrak mS_{\mathfrak m}$-adic completion of $S_{\mathfrak m}=S\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak m}$ and $\prod_{i=1}^t(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge$, where $(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nS_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak q_i^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}$. Since $R$ is local, every element of $R\setminus\mathfrak m$ is a unit, so the localization map $R\to R_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is an isomorphism (injective: $ur=0$ with $u$ a unit gives $r=0$; surjective: $r/u=(ru^{-1})/1$); hence $S\to S\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak m}$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, is a ring isomorphism carrying $\mathfrak mS$ onto $\mathfrak mS_{\mathfrak m}$, and it induces an isomorphism of the $\mathfrak mS$-adic completion of $S$ with the $\mathfrak mS_{\mathfrak m}$-adic completion of $S_{\mathfrak m}$. Composing with the isomorphism $\iota_S$ of Step 3, we obtain a ring isomorphism $\Phi:S\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^t(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge$ (if $t=0$, $S=0$ and the product is the zero ring).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0325, proof, third sentence ('Hence $S$ is the product of the completions at its maximal ideals by Lemma 07N9', lemma-completion-finite-extension, line 23135, with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$ and $R_{\mathfrak m}^\wedge=R$)

proof.text: (Each factor is a complete Noetherian local ring.) Fix $i$ and put $T=S_{\mathfrak q_i}$ and $C_i=T^\wedge$. $T$ is Noetherian as a localization of the Noetherian ring $S$ (Step 1) [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], and local with maximal ideal $I=\mathfrak q_iT$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Hence $C_i$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] (Stacks 05GH), and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_i=IC_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. $I$ is finitely generated since $T$ is Noetherian, so by [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] (1) (with $A=T$, $M=T$) $C_i$ is $I$-adically complete as a $T$-module: $C_i\to\varprojlim_nC_i/I^nC_i$ is bijective; the $T$-submodule $I^nC_i$ is the ideal $(IC_i)^n=\mathfrak n_i^n$ of $C_i$ (as in Step 3), so this is the canonical map of $C_i$ to its $\mathfrak n_i$-adic completion, and $C_i$ is $\mathfrak n_i$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. With Step 4, $S\cong S_1\times\dots\times S_t$ with $S_j=C_j$ Noetherian local rings complete for their maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_j$, and $S$ has finitely many maximal ideals (Step 2); with Step 1 this proves the first assertion.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0325 (statement: 'a product of Noetherian complete local rings'), with Lemma 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian), Lemma 031C (lemma-completion-complete) and Lemma 05GG for the completion of a Noetherian local ring

proof.text:
(The domain case.) Let $S$ be a domain. For an idempotent $e=e^2\in S$ we have $e(1-e)=0$, so $e=0$ or $e=1$. If $t=0$ then $S=0$, impossible for a domain. If $t\ge2$, the element $e=\Phi^{-1}(1,0,\dots,0)$ is an idempotent of $S$ with $e
eq0$ (as $1
eq0$ in the local ring $S_1$) and $e
eq1$ (as $1
eq0$ in $S_2$), a contradiction. So $t=1$ and $\Phi:S	o S_1$ is a ring isomorphism onto a Noetherian local ring. Hence $S$ is a Noetherian local ring; by Step 2 its unique maximal ideal is $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak q_1$, and $\mathfrak q_1$ is the only prime of $S$ whose inverse image in $R$ is $\mathfrak m$. Finally $\Phi(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak n_1$ (the maximal ideal goes to the maximal ideal under a ring isomorphism), so $\Phi(\mathfrak n^k)=\mathfrak n_1^k$ for all $k$ and $\Phi$ induces isomorphisms $S/\mathfrak n^k\cong S_1/\mathfrak n_1^k$ compatible with the projections; under them the canonical map $S	o\varprojlim_kS/\mathfrak n^k$ corresponds to the canonical map $S_1	o\varprojlim_kS_1/\mathfrak n_1^k$, which is bijective by Step 5. So $S$ is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0325 (a domain has no idempotents other than $0,1$, so the product has one factor); the identification of $\mathfrak n$ with the unique prime over $\mathfrak m$ by Step 2 (Lemma 00GS (2))
